Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood PM), Maya (Brightwave Head of Product), Sam (Brightwave Dir ML), Priya (Brightwave Marketing)

Summary: quick recording-style customer interview for marketing. Brightwave talks about switching inference to Redwood for production chat and embedding pipelines; focus on cost savings, latency, and ease of rollout. We capture a few soundbites for the case study and ask permission to quote.

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, this is Aisha from Redwood, we're, we're recording this as a customer interview for marketing, just quick check that the Brightwave folks are ok to be recorded?
[00:05] Maya: yes totally, we signed the consent, excited to share our story
[00:12] Aisha: awesome, i'll kick us off with a couple warm up questions. can you give us a little background on Brightwave and how you use models today?
[00:20] Maya: sure, so Brightwave is a digital marketplace for product discovery, we use models for search relevance, conversational search and for summarization of seller notes. we were on a mix of cloud endpoints and some homegrown infra, we had, you know, a lot of variance in latency and cost, and it was getting hard to predict spend as we scaled
[00:35] Sam: yeah and to add, we had a POC with AlphaAI earlier this year, but the integration was heavier and we couldn't get the latency we needed for our interactive flows
[00:45] [00:47] Liam: quick Q - what were your target SLOs for latency and throughput for the search use case?
[00:50] Maya: for chat we want p95 under 350ms ideally, sometimes 250 if possible, and throughput of about 80 qps during peak with spikes to 150 briefly, we also needed embeddings at scale for ranking batches overnight
[01:05] Aisha: that's super helpful, one thing folks often ask about is deployment mode — you chose Redwood Dedicated, right? can you talk through that?
[01:15] Maya: yeah we started with the hosted API to validate, loved the quick onboarding, but once we moved into production for three core features we committed to Dedicated pools for predictable throughput and also because of data isolation requirements for our enterprise customers
[01:29] Priya: and from marketing perspective, the dedicated part made us feel more confident to say 'we host on private capacity' when we talk to customers, which matters for enterprise logos
[01:38] [01:39] Jordan: can you share the rollout timeline? how long did migration take?
[01:42] Sam: it was about six weeks from initial POC to canary, and full traffic shift in about 10 weeks, that included a week of canarying and two weeks of performance tuning with Redwood SEs
[01:56] Aisha: nice — any surprises during the rollout?
[01:58] Maya: the main surprise was how effective the KV cache was — we saw a 30% token cost reduction on the chat flows after enabling prefix caching, that was bigger than we expected
[02:10] Liam: we also tuned batching and quantization profiles; Sam worked with the ops team to keep p99 stable while reducing GPU costs
[02:18] Sam: yeah, and Redwood's console made it easier to reason about token-level cost, which was important when we had to explain spend to finance
[02:26] Priya: can we get a short, specific soundbite about cost or latency that we can quote? like a sentence or two?
[02:30] Maya: sure — "Switching to Redwood cut our per-interaction inference cost by about a third while improving p95 latency by around 20%"
[02:38] Aisha: love that. we'll include that in the case study, we'll send for sign-off.
[02:42] [02:43] Aisha: next, want to talk about security/compliance since some customers ask about that in marketing collateral
[02:48] Maya: yes, we needed SOC 2 and SSO, we integrated via SAML into our IdP, Redwood's private deployment also hooked into our KMS which was required for certain enterprise contracts
[03:02] Sam: we did ask for audit logs and long-term retention for a few customers, Redwood worked with us to enable the necessary retention window on Dedicated
[03:10] [03:12] Aisha: any comments on the support experience?
[03:14] Maya: the SE support was great — Liam in particular was helpful during the kernel tuning and the canary. we had a runbook for fallback to a smaller model variant during a gpu outage which kept our chat service online
[03:26] Liam: yep that was a fun part — the fallback policy was automated in the routing layer, we had a canary rule and a warm standby model
[03:33] [03:35] Priya: switching to a marketing angle—how has Redwood helped your go-to-market or product storytelling?
[03:39] Maya: we've been able to advertise predictable SLAs and talk about performance numbers in sales calls, that definitely helped close a couple mid-market deals where latency was a differentiator
[03:50] Aisha: perfect, any other product wins you'd like highlighted?
[03:53] Sam: the embeddings pipeline — running batch ranks overnight on Dedicated reduced hours-to-result by 40% vs our previous setup, so recommendation experiments moved faster
[04:04] Jordan: great line for product marketing — "experimentation cadence improved by 40%" maybe we'll run that by you
[04:11] Maya: yes go ahead, we can approve or tweak wording
[04:15] [04:16] Aisha: switching gears — any red flags or things we need to avoid in the case study?
[04:20] Maya: please don't include specific customer names or logos of our enterprise customers — we can speak in aggregate about "enterprise customers". also, avoid quoting internal cost numbers beyond the per-interaction percentage we gave
[04:31] Priya: and please run the final copy by legal; they want to confirm the quote wording
[04:35] Aisha: absolutely, we'll run it for legal approval first.
[04:38] [04:40] Aisha: quick plug — would you be willing to be a guest on a short podcast episode? we can do a 20-minute edited conversation about the migration and product impact
[04:48] Maya: yes we'd love that, Priya will coordinate scheduling and the quote
[04:52] [05:00] (recording stops - ambient chatter while folks confirm availability)
[05:10] Aisha: a couple logistics — we'll need a short bio and a headshot for Promo. Priya?
[05:15] Priya: i'll share a bio and headshot in the next 48 hours
[05:20] Aisha: great. last thing, any technical nitty-gritty people want to call out?
[05:24] Liam: maybe just mention the quantization profile we used — 4-bit for embeddings and 8-bit for chat model, that was part of the cost win but didn't materially affect quality for their prompts
[05:36] Sam: and the routing policy - we used region-first for domestic traffic and cost-aware fallbacks for non-peak to save on GPU spend
[05:45] [05:47] Aisha: ok we're at about 42 minutes, i'll do a quick recap and close out
[05:50] Aisha: recap: we'll produce an edited podcast episode and raw transcript; marketing will draft a short case study blurb and a couple soundbites; Redwood will share benchmark artifacts and latency/cost spreadsheets; Brightwave will provide quote approvals, a bio, and headshot. action items and dates will be in the follow-up email
